messages:
alice: heads-up — dedicated canary c-42 after merge abcdef1 is showing a sustained p95 spike for longseq workloads, roughly 3x baseline. noticed ~02:12 UTC

bob: confirmed on the dashboard. token breakdown points at kernel-selection latency and an uptick in kv cache misses.

carol: started a profiler run. initial traces show heavy mutex contention around KVCache::refill and LRU eviction during prefetch. stack snippet: `KVCache::refill -> LRU::evict -> std::mutex::lock`

deploy-bot: deploy completed for commit abcdef1 (branch: runtime/batch-hints) at 2025-09-04T02:12:12Z. Canaries: c-42, c-48.

dan: doing a bisect on recent merges. quick test: reverting abcdef1 locally restores p95 to expected. that commit changed batching heuristics to prefer merge-kernel in small-batch scenarios.

erin: hypothesis: batching hint change changes request coalescing boundaries, causing shadowed prefetch windows across shards. double-prefetches lead to LRU churn and lock storms. also saw TTL misalignment between prefetch offset and cache expiry.

frank: reproduced with synthetic longseq load at 200 concurrent. flamegraph: `https://perf.internal/fg/1759876543` — kernel-selection and kv LRU traversal dominate CPU. allocator churn also present.

carol: digging deeper: allocation hotspots from vector resize during LRU walk. kernel selection path now executes more frequently per request due to altered batching behavior.

alice: pausing the dedicated rollout for these pools; marking rollout hold and notifying accounts with reserved capacity on c-42. SLA risk if we let this continue.

sre-oncall: acknowledged. filing incident now and paging eng-runtime oncall. incident id INC-20250904-07.

bob: quick mitigation: add per-shard prefetch disable flag and roll a revert of the batching hint commit as a hotpatch. local perf with revert candidate looks promising. patch example: `git revert abcdef1 && cfg.kv_prefetch_per_shard=false`

dan: ran CI perf with revert candidate — p95 and p99 drop back to baseline in our perf pipeline. we should still add a regression test that exercises shadow prefetch windows.

erin: agree. also add a small seq-length distribution stress test to CI to catch this class of regressions.

alice: plan: 1) hold rollout 2) push revert hotpatch to canary pools 3) add unit/CI tests for prefetch window and batching boundaries 4) monitor canary for 1hr before resuming. owner: alice. carol to lead RCA.

everyone: :thumbsup:

alice: I'll draft the postmortem and customer-facing note. any other concerns before I escalate to eng leadership?
